hot.title: Truly Subquadratic 3SUM and Truly Subcubic APSP via Triangles in Sparse Lopsided Graphs
hot.summary: The authors introduce a deterministic algorithm that computes selected entries of a thin matrix product without computing the full product or each entry separately. It recursively multiplies rectangular matrices and prunes work for unrequested outputs. It gives 3SUM in O(n^1.9992) and directed APSP in O(n^2.9995) for polynomially bounded integers in the word-RAM model, asymptotic bounds rather than measured speedups.

hot.title: Introducing Beam: Reflection’s 501B open-weight model
hot.summary: Reflection introduces Beam, its first open-weight model: a sparse Mixture-of-Experts with 501 billion total and 23 billion active parameters, aimed at coding, reasoning, and agentic workloads. It was pretrained on 23.8 trillion curated tokens and then trained with a high-compute reinforcement learning run of over 100 million rollouts on 10.5K NVIDIA GB300 GPUs. Beam is competitive with larger open models while using far less inference compute, and its weights are slated for release under Apache 2.0 later in the month.

hot.title: Kolibri: A Sovereign European Model on the Pareto Frontier
hot.summary: Kolibri is an open-weight bilingual model designed for local deployment on controlled infrastructure. It activates 3.46B of 78.1B parameters per token and uses sliding-window attention in 40 of 50 blocks, with full attention in every fifth block. Against Kolibri Origin, its post-trained scores are higher in English and German, with 2.7× reported decode throughput under the paper’s measurement setup.

hot.title: Base Models Can Reason By Taking a Cue From Training Data
hot.summary: The authors test whether short fixed openings can elicit reasoning from language models without changing their weights. On MATH-500, Olmo-3-7B pass@1 rises from 42% without a cue to 78% with “Okay,” versus 75% after reinforcement learning. In a controlled data-edit experiment, renaming “okay” to “chicken” makes “Chicken” effective, supporting cue effects in these tested settings, not all models.

hot.title: Finetuning with Sampling: SFT Learns Better Than You Think
hot.summary: Projection sampling transforms expert demonstrations into responses more like those of a pretrained model before standard supervised fine-tuning, using the model to propose continuations and an MCMC procedure to select them. On Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, it raises SciKnowEval Chemistry L-3 single-shot accuracy to 66.0%, while the five-task prior-capability average is 58.6%, below the base model’s 59.7%.

hot.title: Quantum minimum description of density matrices
hot.summary: The authors determine the asymptotically minimum memory for reconstructing n copies of a quantum state with known spectrum and hidden eigenbasis. For fixed dimension d and rank r, the leading cost is r(2d-r-1)/2 log₂ n, followed by a spectrum-dependent constant. Their code achieves global error O(log n/√n); a matching converse holds for vanishing-error codes with distinct positive eigenvalues.

hot.title: ThunderSyncRL: Lossless Acceleration of Agentic Reinforcement Learning
hot.summary: ThunderSyncRL streams learner gradient calculations as trajectory rewards or teacher scores become available, while keeping rollouts and gradients tied to one policy snapshot and applying one optimizer step after the batch completes. In the reported Qwen-3.8-27B GRPO setup, it reaches 74.01% pass@3 on SWE-bench Verified in 121.3 GPU-hours versus 233.5 with Sync, a 1.9× speedup; outcomes depend on workload overlap.

hot.title: VISTA: A Visual Harness for Reasoning in an Interactive World
hot.summary: VISTA gives a multimodal model access to archived game frames, allowing it to retrieve earlier images, compare moments, and enlarge details while reasoning in language and choosing actions. Across 25 public ARC-AGI-3 games, Claude Opus 5.0 completes all games with a mean Relative Human Action Efficiency score of 100.00, using 7,302 actions versus 17,135 for first-time humans. This public-set result does not establish performance on unseen games.

hot.title: InterMimicGen: Scaling Humanoid Loco-Manipulation through Self-Evolving Motion Imitation
hot.summary: InterMimicGen expands humanoid motion references by editing object paths or body postures, training a physics-based tracker on edits, and retaining motions that execute in simulation. In a bimanual G1 setting with Inspire hands, references grow 21.8× after round one and 150.5× after round five, while tracker success on accepted references rises from 52.1% to 98.4%. This densifies existing interactions rather than creating new tasks.

hot.title: Priced Guidance: Can Language Models Generate Future Research Ideas?
hot.summary: Priced Guidance measures information needed for a model to recover an existing research idea. A generator assigns probabilities to answers; a target-informed guide selects among them, and less likely answers cost more bits. Expected cost bounds unguided acceptance from below. The ensemble’s median Essence cost was 55.8 bits, versus 69.9 for Fable 5.1 alone, measuring guided recovery rather than independent research generation.

hot.title: LoGo: Local-Global Rewards for Consistent Long-Horizon Video Generation
hot.summary: LoGo trains camera-controlled video models to preserve 3D scene consistency as viewpoints move. It estimates geometry from keyframes, groups pixels into shared 3D voxels, and combines localized reprojection rewards with a global reward. On TrajectoryBench, Lingbot2 reaches PSNR-D 18.2, versus 17.1 for the global-only version, supporting localized credit assignment under this evaluation, not universal physical correctness.

hot.title: Unravelling the Nature of AT\,2025abao: From Precursor to Final Fate
hot.summary: The authors connect AT 2025abao’s eight-year infrared brightening and luminous red nova outburst to a possible common-envelope interaction. Wind-drag modeling favors a 1.4-solar-mass companion to a 6.9-solar-mass asymptotic giant branch star; ejecta models estimate 0.57 solar masses escape. A one-dimensional simulation leaves an eccentric pair after 400 days, but does not establish a surviving compact binary.

hot.title: Multimodal Safety Evaluation Should Measure Controllability Beyond Classification
hot.summary: The authors present a controllability profile to test whether multimodal safety signals are readable, depend on image–text interaction, respond to intervention, and preserve benign behavior. In an implicit-toxicity case study of two models, Qwen3.5’s readout has 3.7% cross-modal specificity, while LlavaGuard shows a narrow benign-preserving clamp range under tested operators; the profile does not certify global safety.

hot.title: Mulligan: Performance-Guided Data Collection for Efficient On-Robot Learning
hot.summary: Mulligan guides robot-learning data collection by choosing some starting states where the policy failed while using coverage-based choices to explore less-tried states. Operators correct and replay tasks, while a critic learns from all rollouts. On Insert Marker, full HiL-IDQL+Mulligan achieved 76% success versus 42% for uniform HG-DAgger; evidence is limited to studied tasks and operator-placeable starts.

hot.title: Free entropy and quantum minimum description length
hot.summary: In free probability, Voiculescu's free entropy counts matrix microstates that approximate an operator. It is a non-commutative analog of the Shannon entropy, distinct from any quantum entropy of a density operator, but it has had no physical meaning in quantum theory. hot.title: One Figure, Every Canvas: Editable Flowchart Relayout via Agentic Pipeline
hot.summary: The authors present a system that converts raster flowcharts into editable graphs and rearranges them for new canvas ratios. It reconstructs components and connections, then applies hierarchical graph layout with critic feedback. Across 500 tasks at five tested ratios, it achieves 68.6% Content Fidelity, versus 41.4% for Nano Banana Pro. This is benchmark evidence, not proof of arbitrary-ratio performance.

hot.title: Closing the Context Gap: Activation Alignment for Tabular In-Context Learning
hot.summary: Activation alignment helps tabular in-context models use fewer training examples at inference by correcting a reduced-context model’s internal representation toward its full-context counterpart. A linear map learns activation differences from synthetic queries processed with full and reduced contexts. At 10% context, it recovers median 48.3% of the teacher–student score gap for TabPFN-3 and 44.7% for TabFM, across classification datasets where the teacher outperforms the unaligned student.

hot.title: I-BFM: Reward-Conditioned Robust Humanoid Interaction via Unsupervised Reinforcement Learning
hot.summary: I-BFM addresses humanoid-object interaction by learning a shared policy that represents robot, object, and contact state and is directed by task rewards. It acts closed-loop rather than following a fixed trajectory. In simulated MuJoCo Carry Box, it achieves 94.3% nominal success and 89.3% after a specified robot fall, versus OmniContact’s 1.3%; these rates are task-completion results under that perturbation.

hot.title: LSTM-Style Looped Transformers with Shared KV Caches
hot.summary: The authors present a recurrent decoder-only transformer that reuses four core blocks across three passes and shares one donor key–value cache across them. A gated update carries state between passes, while late donor-consistency training reduces the width-768 shared-cache continuation penalty from 0.0520 to 0.0099 nats. The cache computations remain unequal, and the result is teacher-forced FineWeb continuation.

hot.title: An FPRAS for Counting Common Bases of Two Matroids
hot.summary: The authors give an FPRAS for counting common bases of two same-rank matroids accessed through independence oracles. Their method samples relaxed pairs of sets, penalizes overlap, and tunes per-element weights so complementary pairs become frequent, then uses sampling to estimate the count. The algorithm runs in Õ(n^13/ε²) time and has the standard 3/4 success probability; the bound is unoptimized.

likes.title: Tokenization: A Survey for Modern NLP
likes.summary: Tokenization is presented as a core language-model design choice that shapes sequence length, computational cost, multilingual equity, evaluation, and security—not merely as preprocessing. The survey reviews established subword methods and emerging byte-level, latent, and visual alternatives, finding that BPE still dominates practice while no tokenizer consistently optimizes compression, linguistic alignment, downstream quality, and crosslingual fairness at once.

likes.title: Towards Looped Models Done Right Part II: Rethinking at Fixed Points
likes.summary: The paper trains a looped language model to settle toward fixed points across repeated applications of a shared block. Terminal key-value (KV) sharing retains only final cache banks; separate methods reuse endpoints for prefill and reinforcement learning. At 1.6B parameters, the learned-depth-prior model scores 60.00% on the downstream average with four rather than twelve KV banks, in the reported setup.

likes.title: Context Language Models
likes.summary: Context Language Models let an agent edit its live conversation by mirroring the transcript into a file whose changes synchronize with subsequent model calls. The approach supports multiple agents and zero-shot context management. On BrowseComp-Plus, Qwen3.6-27B reached 59.4% accuracy, with 21.5% fewer prefix-reuse FLOPs than Codex-style summarization. Results vary by setting and do not isolate editing alone.

likes.title: Looped Diffusion Transformer
likes.summary: Looped-DiT improves text-to-image generation by repeating shared middle Transformer blocks within each denoising step, refining hidden representations without adding unique parameters. Deep Supervision trains intermediate predictions, and Self-Modulating Attention regulates repeated updates. Its B/16 model averages 71.5 across six benchmarks versus 69.0 for 1.7B InternVL-U, at 150 versus 732 TFLOPs per image, in 260M-parameter pixel-space models using 512 × 512 resolution.

likes.title: ScholarCatalyst: A Benchmark for Retrieving Papers That Inspire New Research
likes.summary: ScholarCatalyst benchmarks whether systems can retrieve prior papers that project authors judged helpful or potentially helpful to early-stage research. It uses 894 retrospectively annotated queries from 207 computer-science projects, with author-labeled positives and hard negatives. Across its reported settings, agentic search reaches overall Recall@20 of 0.42 versus 0.48 for embedding retrieval, measuring retrospective judgments rather than successful inspiration.

likes.title: Invent a Dataset: Measuring Dataset Generation Abilities with Zero Seed Data
likes.summary: Invent-a-Dataset generates training examples from a natural-language dataset description, without requiring a seed corpus. The prompt-based API is evaluated on eight requests using quality, semantic diversity, and downstream fine-tuning tests. At 5,000 samples, it scores 7.90 versus 6.76 for Claude Opus 5; at 20,000, diversity is 37% higher than GLM-5.3, but results do not establish universal capability.

likes.title: Gemini 4 Argon: our next era of frontier intelligence
likes.summary: Google DeepMind announces Gemini 4 Argon, a frontier model built to sustain deep reasoning across long, multi-step workflows in software engineering, enterprise knowledge work, and cybersecurity defense. Argon is first rolling out to trusted cyber defenders through the Fairwind Program, with broader API and consumer access to follow after safeguards are strengthened. It launches at an introductory price of $2 / $10 per million input / output tokens.

likes.title: Decoding Looped Transformers Better for (Almost) Free
likes.summary: LoopCD guides looped Transformers by extrapolating from an earlier prediction toward the final prediction for the same prefix, without adding recurrent iterations. It offers logits and hidden-state variants, with hidden-state guidance avoiding an extra output pass. On AIME 2024, adaptive LoopCD-Logits raises Ouro-2.6B-Thinking pass@1 from 61.88% to 73.33%; results are not uniformly positive across tasks and metrics.

likes.title: Sharpening Tax in Post-Training
likes.summary: The authors compare base and post-trained agents on three agentic benchmarks across repeated rollouts, and introduce Sharpening Tax to measure how much success retries recover. For Gemma-4-31B on WebShop, the harness-equipped base model rises from 22.7% pass@1 to 87.6% pass@128, while its post-trained counterpart reaches 39.5% and 56.0%. The comparison is observational and varies by model scale and rollout budget.

likes.title: SkillRefiner: Offline Skill Refinement from Historical Agent Traces
likes.summary: SKILLREFINER refines an agent’s reusable instructions from traces and feedback without generating new executions during refinement. It summarizes and clusters runs by outcome, proposes edits, and checks failure-derived edits against evidence before merging. On 200 held-out SpreadsheetBench tasks, it reached 84.0% accuracy versus 79.0% for Trace2Skill and 78.5% for GEPA; token comparisons exclude collection costs and do not establish computation.

likes.title: PivotOPD: Learning to Recover from Pivotal Mistakes in Multi-Turn Agents
likes.summary: PivotOPD trains multi-turn agents to avoid pivotal mistakes and recover from the states those mistakes create. A teacher supplies gold actions for prevention and recovery responses for later turns, combining these signals with group-based reinforcement learning. On ALFWorld, Qwen3-1.7B reaches 73.7% success versus 68.2% for SDAR; recovery evidence is principally oracle-labeled ALFWorld analysis.

likes.title: Rethinking Representations for World-Action Modeling
likes.summary: ReWAM trains a robot world-action model by using an action-shaped compact visual state and a branch predicting future representations. During training, action gradients shape the state, while world-prediction gradients stop at representations; inference does not generate future states. On RoboTwin 2.0, ReWAM reaches 93.6% random-scene success versus 92.2% for AHA-WAM without generative video pre-training. The result does not establish universality.

likes.title: AnthroDial: Benchmarking LLM Anthropomorphism in Autonomous Social Interaction
likes.summary: AnthroDial gives social agents a private, revisable message draft and scheduled delivery time, allowing them to speak, wait, revise, or cancel as interactions unfold. Its MindFlow harness, CAPS-Eval rubric, and SEEDS–DiAPO training pipeline target timing, continuity, and behaviors. Humans rated the harness more human-like than turn-taking; on Long-Horizon Character, scores reached 0.9930 versus 0.9820, benchmark evidence not real-world social success.

likes.title: Learning Functional Subspaces for Neural Network Compression
likes.summary: LSP compresses neural networks by learning which directions to remove from linear layers rather than local spectra. It trains projectors against output distributions while freezing weights, after allocating ranks using output-KL costs. On Llama-2-7B at 70% compression, LSP reaches 10.9 WikiText-2 perplexity versus 13.3 for SVD-LLM and 222.8 for untrained NoLSP, under reported calibration protocols.

likes.title: Scaling and Distilling Text Embeddings for Better Diffusibility
likes.summary: This paper improves continuous diffusion language models by distilling a smaller encoder to preserve a teacher’s probabilities over plausible next words, bringing their embeddings closer. On OWT-1024, ELF-M reaches generated-text perplexity 17.8±0.1 at entropy 5.45±0.01, versus 19.3±0.2 for raw T5Gemma-2, using 512 rather than 256 denoiser evaluations. This quality comparison is not at equal compute.

likes.title: Trust the Critic More
likes.summary: AC2 trains proof-solving language models from unfinished proofs by resuming saved prefixes, generating bounded chunks, and using a learned critic to estimate eventual rubric scores. A readiness gate permits critic-based updates only for problems where its estimates are sufficiently reliable; others use terminal rewards. On IMO-ProofBench, AC2 reached GRPO’s peak mean score with 2.5× fewer decoding FLOPs, within the reported repeated-data setup.
